findings.text: non-blocking: reckon/crew/prompts.py:662 adds with_claude_anchored_edit_instruction beside the existing owner with_anchored_edit_instruction at line 621. Both functions do the same thing — append ANCHORED_EDIT_HEADING body to a prompt after rstripping it — and differ only in the body text and in which dialect they admit; the owner already takes a backend and gates on a dialect, so it could have carried a claude body. The duplication is small (one f-string and a docstring) and the constant is shared, so the cost is drift rather than a second mechanism, but a later change to the heading or the append framing now has two sites to update.

findings.summary: the new anchored instruction is appended without stripping one the incoming prompt already carries, unlike the figure listing three lines above at line 3101 which strips for exactly this reason, so a prompt composed from a run's stored prompt.txt and re-launched on a seeding Claude lane gains a second copy of the instruction
findings.text: non-blocking: reckon/_backends.py:3115 appends the anchored instruction unconditionally where the prompt already may carry one. The same function strips a figure listing first (line 3101, with its rationale at line 2880: 'a lane change composes from the run's prompt file, which a fresh dispatch has already written with a listing') precisely so a second copy is never handed over, and the new append has no equivalent strip. A re-launch whose prompt comes from a store that already holds the instruction therefore carries it twice; the effect is cosmetic rather than harmful, because a repeated instruction is idempotent, which is why this does not hold the node.
